summary.text: An acid–base reaction is a chemical reaction that happens between an acid and a base.
In the Brønsted–Lowry view, an acid–base reaction removes a proton from the acid and adds it to the base.
Several theories define acids and bases, and they complement each other: Lewis is the broadest and Arrhenius the most restrictive.

facts.label: Conjugate base
facts.value: The acid with a proton removed

facts.label: Arrhenius acid
facts.value: Ionises in water to form hydrogen cations

facts.label: Arrhenius limit
facts.value: Only applies to substances in water

facts.label: Brønsted–Lowry year
facts.value: Formulated in 1923 by Brønsted and Lowry

facts.label: Brønsted–Lowry idea
facts.value: Acids donate protons; bases accept them

items.prompt: A base takes a proton from an acid in a reaction. What has the base turned into?

options.label: A salt that can no longer react
A stronger base with a larger charge
Its conjugate acid, the base with a proton added
The solvent that the proton was dissolved in

items.explain: Receiving a proton gives the base its conjugate acid, which is the base with a proton added.

items.prompt: A chemist uses Arrhenius's idea to decide whether a dissolved substance is a base. What must it do to count?

options.label: Raise the concentration of hydrogen ions in the solution
Raise the concentration of hydroxide ions in the solution
Accept a proton handed over by another molecule
Accept an electron pair to form a new bond

items.explain: An Arrhenius base increases hydroxide ions in an aqueous solution. Raising hydrogen ions defines an Arrhenius acid.

items.prompt: Pure HCl dissolved in toluene is not acidic by Arrhenius's definition. What limit of that definition explains this?

options.label: It only covers acids that contain a metal atom
It only covers reactions that give off heat
It only covers acids that have no hydrogen in them
It only covers substances that are dissolved in water

items.explain: Arrhenius's definition is restricted to aqueous solutions, so it fails for non-aqueous cases like HCl in toluene. That led to the Brønsted–Lowry and Lewis theories.

items.prompt: In a reaction, one molecule hands a hydrogen cation to a second molecule. In the Brønsted–Lowry view, what is the first molecule?

options.label: The acid, because it donates the proton
The base, because it donates the proton
The salt, because it carries the proton
The solvent, because it holds the proton

items.explain: Brønsted–Lowry acids donate hydrogen cations (protons) and bases accept them.

items.prompt: A student says the Arrhenius, Brønsted–Lowry and Lewis theories contradict each other, so only one can be right. What is the better view?

options.label: Arrhenius is the correct one and the later ones are mistakes
Lewis is the narrowest, so the others replaced it
They complement each other, from Lewis as broadest to Arrhenius as narrowest
They apply in different centuries and are now all retired

items.explain: The models complement each other. Lewis has the broadest definition, Brønsted–Lowry is a subset of it, and Arrhenius is the most restrictive.

items.prompt: A cake batter rises in the oven after baking powder meets water. What makes the bubbles?

options.label: Baking soda and acidic salts react and release carbon dioxide gas
Baking soda alone boils away as steam in the heat
The acidic salts burn off as a cloud of smoke
The liquid splits apart into hydrogen and oxygen gas

items.explain: Baking powder is baking soda plus acidic salts. With water, they react to give gaseous carbon dioxide, which forms the bubbles.
